answer: Latency triangulation stops sybils by fingerprinting each identity's network position. Five dispersed lantern beacons send timed challenges; the node answers from its kernel stack, and each beacon records latency and jitter into a unique vector. Genuine nodes produce distinct vectors, like footprints across a dune field; clones behind one host return near-identical vectors and are flagged. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 distinct egress points at $5-20 per month each. Limits: VPNs blur vectors and CGNAT users share paths, so flagged identities face a bond challenge and audit.
